# Independent audit: sampled touching majorants and fixed-mark logarithmic bound

Source audited in full:
`candidate 87de5b3c068291f1`.
Result: PASS. Independently reran its verifier: 18,641 exact calibration checks.
No repair identified. The hypotheses include actual compatible positive fibers,
an old finite contact certificate, and interior-uniform convergence of the
current normalized concave parameters.

## 1. Sampled support planes and bounded base slopes

The own-fiber supergradient exists at an interior mark and gives exact equality
phi_p=U(Y)-c.y. For any anchored representation of p, actual Minkowski inclusion
places the convex combination of chosen maximizers in K_p. Concavity then gives
phi_p>=sum lambda phi_z. This is precisely the finite Farkas condition for the
sampled base-slope inequalities, including boundary bases and lower affine rank.
No ambient supporting plane at the marked real-base boundary is presumed.

The minimum-norm feasible slope bound is proved correctly. Its vector lies in
the conic hull of active inward constraint normals. Reduce that representation
to linearly independent active rows. The vector lies in their row span and
satisfies their active equalities, giving
N_I^T(N_I N_I^T)^(-1)d_I. The finitely many fixed row submatrices give a uniform
bound even when active sets switch. Zero rows cause no difficulty.

## 2. Moving majorants and boundary uniformity

Positivity and concavity about a fixed inner ball bound each sampled maximum
by a constant times its value at one fixed interior point. The assumed interior
convergence thus supplies the required global sampled bound. Source interior
balls bound every chosen continuous supergradient; the preceding finite LP
then bounds the base gradients. These facts control every coefficient of the
finite plane array.

The minimum of the planes majorizes U_t only where required, on the sampled
fibers, and touches EVERY listed source because its own plane touches and all
other planes majorize there. Each constituent plane is positive on S_t, hence
on its convex hull by affinity. Ambient majorization of U_t is unnecessary.

Every coefficient-subsequence limit V majorizes L on sampled interiors and,
by continuity, on their boundaries. It equals L at all source marks. Applying
the unnormalized old contact inequality gives mean log(V/L)<=0, while pointwise
majorization gives the opposite inequality. Thus V=L on all sampled fibers.
This proves uniform sampled convergence of the MAJORANTS and a common positive
floor; it does not assert boundary convergence of U_t. Uniformly bounded slopes
extend the convergence to the current fibers under Hausdorff comparison.

## 3. Signed normalization and the fixed old marks

The exact finite inequalities have the correct direction:

    sum sigma log(U_t(Y_i)/L_i)
       >=mean_old log V_t
       >=[integral_old log V_t-integral_current log V_t]/M.

The second step uses current normalization and V_t>=U_t on S_t, so the current
integral of log V_t is nonnegative. No moving source mark, row contraction,
or normalization of V_t is inserted.

For a signed radial path the sampled symmetric difference is O(t). Uniform
convergence and a positive floor permit replacing log V_t in the difference
by the fixed continuous reference log L with o(t) error. The ordinary oriented
shell formula then gives +t integral_boundary log L v for old minus current
integrals, where v is inward normal speed. Therefore the coefficient s(v) has
the stated positive sign. Both outward pieces and d=1 endpoint counting are
included correctly.

## 4. Scope and calibrations

The sampled sqrt-base example correctly demonstrates why the support LP must
not be replaced by an ambient-supergradient assertion. The downward boundary
layer has the advertised constant touching majorant and does not obstruct its
uniform convergence. In the affine interval calibration I independently checked
rho normalization, its mean y=2/log3-2, L(y)=c/log3, and the signed derivative
-h log3/2 on both sides of the inequality.

The fixed-mark scalar lower envelope follows from actual proper-gap scalar
inversion and the displayed logarithmic inequality. The source retains the
remaining inverse-response expansion as an ADDITIONAL hypothesis. It does not
claim an optimized derivative, equality of surface and volume couplings, or
any Gamma estimate.

## 5. Distinct entropy consequence

The companion result
`candidate 0e1bf4bac5d35265`
uses this geometric majorant construction but supplies a different compactness
input: bounded marked values control sampled maxima by the existing volume
rows and barycenter-preserving conditional contractions. It therefore proves
local entropy attainment without assuming optimized-buffer continuity. This
is a separate argument, not an extra unstated hypothesis of the source audited
here.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
